findings.reason: §17 must state that generalisation or those three walks cannot be absorbed and remain duplicates.
findings.text: §17 requires "every heading walk in the package" to call the section reader, but the reader it names yields h2 only, while `evidence._section_labels` (`reckon/evidence.py:65`, `find_all(re.compile(r"^h[1-6]$"))` and reads each heading's text and level), `routing._contains_plan_section` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:2481`, same regex) and `dispatch` section resolution (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:334`, matches h1–h6 and uses the level to bound sibling collection) genuinely consume all levels; a consolidation onto an h2-only reader silently narrows those three, so the parser must be generalised to every heading level and to yield heading text and level, a change §17 does not state.

findings.reason: the section must name the public reader it exposes to other packages or say why the widened public reader is not a new counted definition.
findings.text: §17's interface accounting claims no public definition is added and that the parser keeps its name, but five module-crossing consumers cannot import the private `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`, so either an existing public entry (`structured_section_spans`, whose current return is spans only) must widen its contract to carry identity, heading text and the landed flag, or a new public reader is added and counted; §17 names neither, and §18's own house rule ("a definition consumed across a package boundary earns a public name") makes this a public-surface addition §17 must account for.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §17's "one raw-text section reader" is specified as the existing h2-only `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44`, `handle_starttag` matches `tag == "h2"` and `_H2_OPEN_RE` only), yet three of the walks it must absorb match every level h1–h6.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names the duplicate owners and consolidates them rather than forking: the two `c-run-` spellings (`promotion._LANDING_COMMENT_PREFIX`, `plan_review.RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX`) and the two landing recognisers move to one home in §18, and the heading walks consolidate onto the parser in §17.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §17 rewrites module-crossing consumers (top-level `doccheck`, `mcp_views`, `evidence` plus crew `routing`, `dispatch`) onto a private parser while its own accounting states "no public definition is added; the parser keeps its name", leaving the public entry point that carries section identity and the landed flag unnamed.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16 extends the existing whole-document digest (`plan_fingerprint`/`_fingerprint_forms`), §17 consolidates onto the existing raw-text `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` and its AST-rule precedent `_staged_writes` in `reckon/interface_counts.py` (verified present and test-consumed), and §18 names the two existing readers (`promotion._plan_remaining_sections`, `doccheck._implementable_section_ids`) before hoisting one; each new mechanism cites the file it extends rather than proposing a subsystem.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 states in its own text why the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (one record vs a set of outstanding sections joined to a union of digests), and §17/§18 each justify their consolidation against the mechanism they replace rather than layering over it.
